title: [D9 Operations] Durability, backup and single-store correctness
summary: The single store now has a stated durability model and an executable backup and restore. `src/helena/durability.py` reads the durable relation set from the engine's catalogue and writes a logical backup as header / one row per line / trailer, with the body digest in the trailer so truncation is visible; `restore` refuses before its first INSERT and rebuilds materialized views from the migrations rather than restoring them. `scripts/backup.py` (`--out` / `--verify` / `--restore`, plus `make backup`) is the operator surface, `docs/runbook.md` §15 the procedure and `docs/decisions/0040-durability-and-backup.md` the model with its exclusions. The startup check found a real defect on the way: `scan_captures` returned `{}` for a missing directory, a file and an empty directory alike, so a mistyped `--captures` read as 'this deployment retained no captures' — now `helena.normalizer.CaptureStoreUnreachable`.
assumption_validated: THAT THE SINGLE-STORE RULE SURVIVES ITS OWN RECOVERY STORY — that findings and evidence living only in the streaming engine can be backed up and restored without a second store, and that what a restore cannot bring back is nameable rather than discovered later. It can, and `tests/test_durability.py` is the rehearsal: a full pipeline state built across the broker and the engine, backed up from one migrated schema, restored into another, every relation compared. The key measurement is a negative one and is the point of the increment: A CAPTURE REPLAY ALONE RECONSTRUCTS THE INPUT AND NO ASSESSMENT, SNAPSHOT OR EVIDENCE ROW. The retained captures are not a backup of the store; they are a backup of the store's INPUT, and the difference is the whole reason the engine has to be backed up at all. NOT VALIDATED: no restore has been rehearsed against a store larger than a fixture, and the recovery times recorded (~24 s for the fixture state, ~27 s for a 3 375-claim snapshot) are dominated by applying the migrations rather than by moving the data, so they do not extrapolate.
makes_buildable: Task 54 and 55 get the durability model as a written record rather than an assumption: docs/decisions/0040 names the exclusions (the broker retains nothing that can be relied on, the output topic is egress) so the hazard register task 55 writes can cite a decision instead of restating the argument. `CaptureStoreUnreachable` gives task 55's deferred-register check the same shape it needs — a typed refusal where an empty result used to be.

verification.detail: 1858 passed, 1 skipped in 958 s on the final tree. The skip is tests/test_analyst.py:1725, the live analyst run, whose configured model returned `timed_out` this time — model behaviour, and the same flake task 51 recorded as `schema_invalid` on one run and green the next. `uv run pytest -q tests/test_durability.py` alone is 26 passed in 112 s; `uv lock --check` resolves 17 packages unchanged and `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` is clean. NO DEPENDENCY WAS ADDED. THE SESSION THAT WROTE THIS CODE DID NOT VERIFY IT — see `failed_approaches`; the run above, the two corrections below and the landing were done by a later session. THE RESTORE ORDERING FIX WAS PROVED TO BITE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: with the pre-fix loop restored, test_a_per_relation_count_that_disagrees_refuses_before_any_insert fails naming helena_analytical_assessment, helena_analytical_run_metrics and helena_analytical_escalation_counts as rows a REFUSED restore had written; with the fix it passes. The test needs an explicit FLUSH before reading the target, because without one the writes are real but not yet visible and the test passes against broken code — which it did on its first run, and is why the FLUSH is in it.

deferred: Folding `read_header` into `verify`. The session that wrote the module listed this among the refinements it had staged and never applied. It is a factoring preference, `read_header` is in `__all__` and used, and `concept/instruction.md` §3 leaves factoring to the session doing the work — so guessing at another session's intent here would be a change with no stated reason. Deliberately not done.

A server-side cursor for `back_up`. `_read` iterates a client-side psycopg cursor, which materializes a relation's whole result set, so peak memory is the largest single relation rather than the largest single row. `connection.cursor(name=…)` would change that and is a change to MEASURE rather than to assume; the largest relation here is a 3 375-claim snapshot and fits comfortably. The docstring now states the limit instead of claiming it away.
A restore rehearsed at production scale. The recorded recovery times are fixture-scale and migration-dominated, and `docs/runbook.md` §15 says so rather than extrapolating them.
lessons: A REFUSAL THAT FIRES AFTER THE FIRST INSERT IS NOT A REFUSAL. `restore`'s docstring says 'every refusal here fires before one', and the per-relation row-count check was nonetheless written inside the same loop that inserts, so a disagreement on a later relation left the earlier ones written and the engine has no transaction to roll that back. Validate every relation, then insert every relation: two loops, and the ordering is the invariant rather than a style choice. A docstring stating an invariant is not evidence the code holds it.

WHEN ASSERTING THAT A REFUSED WRITE WROTE NOTHING TO RISINGWAVE, `FLUSH` FIRST. The rows a half-completed restore inserted are not visible to a later read until a FLUSH, so the obvious form of the test passes against the broken code. This one did, and only found the bug once the FLUSH was added — measure the store, not the store's visible prefix.

`contents()` READS VIEWS TOO, so 'the schema is untouched' cannot be written as 'every relation is empty': `helena_aggregation_version` and `helena_retention_horizon` are views over a constant and have rows in a schema nothing has ever written to. Compare against a snapshot taken before the operation, which is what the neighbouring refusal test already did.

`scan_captures` globbing a path that is not there returned `{}`, and a glob cannot tell 'no captures' from 'no directory'. That is `concept/instruction.md` §2's 'absence is not emptiness' in the one place nobody looked for it — an operator-supplied path. The general form: any function whose 'nothing found' answer comes from a glob, a filter or a LEFT JOIN owes the caller a distinction between an empty container and a missing one.
failed_approaches: task 53: ENDING THE SESSION'S TURN TO WAIT FOR A BACKGROUND TEST RUN. This is what made the task fail, and it cost a $16 session that had already finished the work. The session started the ~14-minute suite in the background and ended its turn saying 'a background watcher will re-invoke me when it finishes; I'll then apply the final refinements I've staged, re-run the suite, write the report, and commit'. NOTHING RE-INVOKES A HEADLESS `claude -p` SESSION: implement.sh runs one non-interactive session and the turn ending IS the session ending. The envelope recorded stop_reason 'end_turn', terminal_reason 'completed', is_error false, exit code 0 and no report, so the runner correctly scored it `failed` while the whole increment sat uncommitted in the working tree. RUN THE SUITE IN THE FOREGROUND AND WAIT FOR IT, even though it takes fifteen minutes. Never end a turn intending to be woken up. This is a different failure from task 48's (SIGTERM, zero-byte log) and has a different fix.

task 53: Asserting 'a refused restore wrote nothing' as `not any(rows for rows in contents(target).values())`. It fails against CORRECT code, because `contents` includes views over constants that always have rows. Compare before and after instead.
next_session_should_know: The single store has a backup, a restore and a rehearsal, and the durability model is written down. FIVE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE ENTRY POINTS ARE `make backup` / `scripts/backup.py` with `--out`, `--verify` and `--restore [--schema]`, and `helena.durability` beneath them: `durable_relations(connection)`, `back_up(connection, *, taken_at) -> Iterator[str]`, `verify(lines) -> BackupHeader`, `restore(connection, lines) -> RestoreResult`. The format is header line, one row per line, trailer — and the trailer carries the body digest BECAUSE it is at the end, which is what makes a truncated file detectable rather than merely short. (2) WHAT A RESTORE DOES NOT BRING BACK IS THE POINT, NOT A GAP. Materialized views are rebuilt by the migrations (`RESTORE_REBUILDS`), never restored, and the retained captures reconstruct the INPUT only: `test_a_replay_without_a_restore_does_not_bring_back_an_assessment` is that measured. The broker and the output topic are excluded from the durability model by decision, in docs/decisions/0040. (3) EVERY REFUSAL IN `restore` FIRES BEFORE THE FIRST INSERT and the ordering is load-bearing, because the engine has no transaction around a multi-statement write. This was a real bug, found and fixed during landing, and there is now a test that goes red if the validation moves back inside the insert loop. If you add a check to `restore`, put it in the validation phase. (4) A TEST THAT READS THE ENGINE AFTER A REFUSED WRITE MUST `FLUSH` FIRST, or it passes against broken code. (5) `scan_captures` NOW RAISES `CaptureStoreUnreachable` instead of returning `{}` for a path that is not a readable directory — `helena.status` can now tell 'retained nothing' from 'was never opened', and docs/runbook.md §13.1 explains why it refuses to print that zero.
